nodes.title: Revisions
nodes.body:
June 15, 1993.   T.D. Phillips; Mote Marine Laboratory

OTHER COMMON NAMES - Gulf black sea bass (327 834), seabass (312 664), blackfish (312 581 834 876), black will (312 834).

nodes.title: CLASSIFICATION
nodes.body:
Phylum:  Chordata
	Class:  Osteichthys
	Order:  Perciformes
	Family:  Serranidae

nodes.title: VALUE
nodes.body:
Commercial:  Historically caught by handline in the Chesapeake and supported a fishery which landed 5,100 lbs. in 1920 (312).  Also caught for market in North Carolina (834).  An important commercial resource in the south Atlantic bight (881 882), with 1000 metric tons landed in 1967 (883).

Recreational:  Supports a large sport fishery (312) and is an important recreational resource in the south Atlantic bight (881 882) because it is ?well flavored? (312).

nodes.title: RANGE
nodes.body: Overall:  Occurs from Maine to northeast Florida and in the eastern Gulf of Mexico.  Reaches extreme south Florida in cold winters (788).

nodes.title: By State
nodes.body: Within Study Area:  On east coast of Florida to Indian River lagoon.  Florida west coast south to Charlotte Harbor (879).

nodes.title: Life Mode
nodes.body: Eggs and larvae are pelagic (841 880). Larvae become demersal at about 13 mm and also become estuarine (880).  Adults are demersal.

nodes.title: Habitat Type
nodes.body: Substrate:  Juveniles of 25 to 35 mm found in eel grass (868).  Adults found near rock jetties or over rocky bottoms (788), over rock or shell (581), around pilings of wharves (312), and in rough coral and sea fans (834).

nodes.title: Eggs
nodes.body:
Larvae:  Collected at temperatures from 14.3 to 28 C at the surface, and from 8.3 to 26.6 C at the bottom (868).

Juvenile/adults:  Juveniles recorded from 13.5 C (886) to 31 C (887).  In Charlotte Harbor, collected from 20 C to 32 C (789).  Temperature range reported as from 8.0 C (51) to 29.8 C (885).  Rarely found below 10 C (879).

nodes.title: Eggs
nodes.body:
Larvae:  Larvae collected at salinities ranging from 30.3 to 34.6 % (868).

Juvenile/adults:  Salinities for juveniles range from 30.5 % (886) to 36.6 % (887).  Adults were collected in Charlotte Harbor from 16 % to 32.7 % (789).  Minimum salinity for adults is reported as 7.7 % (868).

nodes.title: MOVEMENTS/MIGRATIONS
nodes.body: Juveniles are reported to leave estuaries in the fall and return in the spring (880).  In Virginia, adults move southeast and offshore in the fall, and migrate northward and inshore in the spring (876).  A gradual offshore movement with age has been demonstrated (876).  Average age at 10-14 fathoms is 2.4 years compared to 4.8 years at 20-25 fathoms (876).  Males are more abundant at 20-25 fathoms than females (876).  In the south they are more or less stationary with tagged individuals caught in the same area as released from 8 to 341 days later (38).

nodes.title: REPRODUCTION
nodes.body:
Repro Mode:  Reproduction is sexual with external broadcast spawning.  Protogynous hermaphrodite with sexual transformation from female to male at age 1-5 (877 878).  Most commonly, transition occurs at age 3 (876).

Mating & spawning:  Most females are mature at age 3 (878).  Males develop a bright blue hump on the nape during spawning (312 834).  Known as a multiple spawner (878).  Spawning occurs in offshore coastal waters (834 880 889).  Spawning occurs in May in North Carolina (834); June through October in Virginia (878).  A northward progression of the spawning season has been reported (868).  A late winter or early spring spawning period was reported at Cedar Key (581).  Hoff (890) reported a February through April spawning period in Florida.

Reproductive capacity:  Fecundidty ranges from 127,000 to 330,000 in the mid-Atlantic bight, and from 29,770 to 121,500 in South Carolina (876 878).

nodes.title: GROWTH & DEVELOPMENT
nodes.body:
Eggs:  Eggs hatch in 75 hours at 15.5 C (841).

Larvae:  Larval development is described by Hardy (868).

nodes.title: Juveniles
nodes.body:
Adults:  Reaches maximum length of 60 or 61 cm (51 788).  The length to weight relationship for fish of both sexes has been reported as:
[eq]
log W = -4.48326 + 2.98699 log (SL), weight in grams and length in mm, r=.99, n=1771 (876).
[/eq]

nodes.title: FOOD & FEEDING
nodes.body: Young feed on shrimp, isopods, and amphipods (312).  Adult diet is chiefly crabs and fish (312).  Also feeds on shrimp, squid, mollusks, and plants (312 581 834).
